mainTopic: The sin and punishment of עכן, יהושע's bold words to ה׳, and יהושע's meeting with the captain of ה׳'s army
overview: This amud continues the story of עכן, who took from the חרם at יריחו. First the גמרא explains that the nation was punished because his sin was not hidden: his wife and children knew. It then draws lessons from the פסוקים in יהושע 7. A Jew who sins is still called ישראל. The five times 'גם' appears show that עכן broke all five חומשי תורה. Other teachings show that he hid his מילה and sinned with a נערה המאורסה, and רבינא says the link to that case teaches that his punishment was סקילה. רב הונא explains that עכן's children were brought along only to watch and learn, not to be killed. The גמרא then discusses how יהושע spoke boldly to ה׳ after the loss at העי, and how ה׳ answered him. The amud ends by explaining why יהושע could bow to a stranger at night: the stranger used ה׳'s name, and שדים do not say ה׳'s name for nothing.

steps.title: Why was the nation punished for עכן's sin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the people were punished for עכן's sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: עכן: what is the reason they were punished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the nation was held responsible for what עכן did. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question comes from the earlier discussion, which taught that the nation is not punished for sins that are hidden from view. עכן's theft seems to have been a hidden sin, so it is surprising that everyone suffered for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The man who secretly took from the forbidden spoils of יְרִיחוֹ

phrases.english: Achan: what is the reason they were punished?
phrases.notes: The earlier discussion said the nation isn't punished for hidden sins, so why did everyone suffer for עכן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about punishment for hidden sins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the nation was punished for עכן's sin if hidden sins do not bring punishment on the whole nation.

steps.title: His wife and children knew
steps.stepSummary: The sin was not truly hidden, because עכן's wife and children knew about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because his wife and his children knew about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that עכן's sin was not really hidden, because his family knew about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once other people knew about the sin, it was no longer a 'hidden' matter. That is why the rule protecting the nation from punishment for hidden sins did not apply here.
steps.whatToRemember: A sin that other people know about is not considered 'hidden,' so the nation can be held responsible for it.

phrases.english: Because they knew about it
his wife and his children.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דַּהֲווֹ יָדְעִי בֵּיהּ אִשְׁתּוֹ וּבָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sin was known to his wife and children, so it was not a hidden sin.

steps.title: Even when sinning, a Jew is still called ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר זבדא learns from 'חטא ישראל' that a Jew who sins is still ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Israel has sinned.' רבי אבא בר זבדא said: even though he sinned, he is still ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new phrase from the פסוק, 'חטא ישראל,' and רבי אבא בר זבדא learns a lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have described the sinners with a harsher name. By still calling them 'ישראל' in the middle of describing their sin, the פסוק shows that sinning does not cancel a Jew's identity.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for the idea that a Jew who sins still remains a Jew.

phrases.english: "Israel has sinned."
phrases.notes: יהושע 7:11

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא, יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא.
phrases.english: Even though he sinned, he is Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל. אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new teaching drawn from the פסוק about עכן's sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew who sins is still called ישראל.

steps.title: The myrtle among other plants
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא supports the idea with a folk saying: a myrtle stays a myrtle even when it grows among other plants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: this is what people say: a myrtle standing among willows is still named a myrtle, and people call it a myrtle.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא backs up the previous teaching with a common saying people use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The myrtle stands for the Jew, and the plants around it stand for sin or bad surroundings. Just as the myrtle keeps its name and value wherever it grows, a Jew keeps the name ישראל even when he sins.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (introduces a folk saying)
Willows (some explain it as thorns): lesser plants

steps.whatToRemember: A Jew who sins is still called ישראל, just as a myrtle keeps its name wherever it grows.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
This is what people say:
A myrtle that stands among willows,
its name is myrtle, and people call it myrtle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבא בר זבדא's teaching with a folk saying.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a Jew who sins remains ישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The popular saying about a myrtle among willows.

steps.title: עכן violated all five חומשי תורה
steps.stepSummary: Because 'גם' appears five times in the פסוק, רבי אילעא learns that עכן violated all five חומשי תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They have also transgressed My covenant which I commanded them, and also taken from the חרם, and also stolen, and also denied, and also put it among their belongings.' רבי אילעא said in the name of רבי יהודה בר מספרתא: this teaches that עכן transgressed the five books of the Torah, since 'גם' (also) is said five times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rest of the פסוק, and רבי אילעא learns from the repeated word 'גם' how widespread עכן's sin was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word 'גם' five times, and each 'גם' is read as hinting at one of the five חומשים. So עכן's sin is described as going against the entire תורה, not just one rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Property dedicated to ה׳ and forbidden for personal use
The five books of the תורה

phrases.english: "And they have also transgressed My covenant
phrases.notes: יהושע 7:11, the same פסוק as before

phrases.english: which I commanded them,
and they have also taken from the dedicated property,
and also stolen, and also denied,
and also put it among their own belongings."
Rabbi Ile'a said
in the name of Rabbi Yehuda bar Masparta:
This teaches that Achan transgressed
the five books of the Torah,
as "also" is said five times.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר מַסְפַּרְתָּא: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁעָבַר עָכָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues expounding the same פסוק with a new teaching about עכן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The five times 'גם' appears hint that עכן violated all five חומשי תורה.

steps.title: עכן tried to hide his ברית מילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא also teaches that עכן tried to undo the sign of his מילה, learning this from the shared word 'בריתי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אילעא said in the name of רבי יהודה בר מספרתא: עכן would stretch his foreskin. It is written here 'they have also transgressed My covenant,' and it is written there 'he has broken My covenant.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching from the same רבי אילעא adds another sin to עכן's record. It is proven by linking two פסוקים that use the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'אֶת בְּרִיתִי' in יהושע is linked to 'אֶת בְּרִיתִי הֵפַר' in בראשית, which speaks about מילה. This link shows that the 'covenant' עכן broke includes the covenant of מילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Stretching the remaining foreskin to hide that he was circumcised
'It is written here… and it is written there' (linking two פסוקים by a shared word)

steps.whatToRemember: The phrase 'גם עברו את בריתי' shows two things about עכן: he went against all five books of the Torah, and he tried to hide his ברית מילה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ile'a said
in the name of Rabbi Yehuda bar Masparta:
Achan would stretch his foreskin.
phrases.notes: He means עכן tried to make himself look uncircumcised, hiding the sign of his מילה.

phrases.english: It is written here: "And they have also transgressed My covenant,"
and it is written there: "He has broken My covenant."
phrases.notes: בראשית 17:14, a פסוק about מילה

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר מַסְפַּרְתָּא: עָכָן מוֹשֵׁךְ בְּעׇרְלָתוֹ הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same speaker, using the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עכן tried to hide his ברית מילה, learned by linking 'בריתי' in יהושע with 'בריתי' in בראשית.

steps.title: Isn't the teaching about מילה obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אילעא needed to teach that עכן undid his מילה, since he already said עכן broke the whole תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אילעא's teaching from step 6. If עכן broke all five חומשי תורה, then of course he also broke the מצוה of מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 already said עכן broke all five חומשי תורה. That sounds like it covers every מצוה. So why did רבי אילעא need a separate teaching about מילה?

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! The גמרא says this when a teaching seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: That's obvious!
phrases.notes: Obvious because רבי אילעא already said עכן broke all five חומשים, so מילה should be included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether step 6 adds anything beyond step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילעא's teaching that עכן undid his מילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general statement that he broke all five חומשים already includes מילה, so the specific teaching seems to add nothing.

steps.title: A מצוה on his own body is a different level
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought that even עכן would not reject a מצוה carried on his own body, so רבי אילעא had to teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: with a מצוה on his own body, he did not throw off the yoke. So it teaches us that he did.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7. Without רבי אילעא's teaching, we might have thought מילה was an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking many מצוות is one thing. Erasing the sign of the ברית from your own body is a deeper kind of rejection. Someone might think even עכן held back from that, so the teaching was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken idea the גמרא wants to rule out).
So it teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong).
He acted irreverently; he threw off the yoke.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the standard way the גמרא answers 'פשיטא': there was a reasonable mistake to rule out. The same pattern comes right back in steps 11 and 12.

phrases.english: You might have said:
with a מצוה of his own body he did not act irreverently?
phrases.notes: Literally 'a מצוה of his body,' meaning מילה, which is done on the body itself.

phrases.english: So it teaches us (that he did).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ruling out a mistaken assumption (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even עכן would not reject a מצוה carried on his own body.
steps.terutzMaskana: He rejected even מילה, so רבי אילעא's teaching adds real information.

steps.title: עכן was with a נערה המאורסה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר זבדא learns from the words 'he did a נבלה in ישראל' that עכן was with a betrothed girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And because he did a disgraceful act in ישראל.' רבי אבא בר זבדא said: This teaches that עכן had relations with a betrothed young woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר זבדא adds another sin to עכן's list. He reads the word 'נבלה' in the פסוק as pointing to a נערה המאורסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes עכן's act as a 'נבלה,' a disgraceful act. רבי אבא בר זבדא says this word points to an additional sin, an איסור of עריות. The source for this reading comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed young woman (after אירוסין, before נישואין)

phrases.english: "And because he did a disgraceful act in ישראל."
phrases.notes: יהושע 7:15

phrases.english: רבי אבא בר זבדא said:
This teaches that עכן had relations with
a betrothed young woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new drasha about another sin of עכן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'נבלה' of עכן was relations with a נערה המאורסה.

steps.title: The shared word 'נבלה' links the two פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: The same phrase 'עשה נבלה בישראל' appears about עכן and about a נערה המאורסה who sinned, which ties the two together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says 'and because he did a disgraceful act,' and there it says 'because she did a disgraceful act in ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the source for רבי אבא בר זבדא's teaching. The same words appear in two places, so the two cases are linked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים about a נערה המאורסה uses the exact words 'עשתה נבלה בישראל.' Because עכן's פסוק uses the same words, a גזירה שוה connects them. That connection is what makes his 'נבלה' the sin of a נערה המאורסה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here (in the case we are discussing)
It is written there (in the other source)
Linking two פסוקים through a shared word or phrase

phrases.english: It is written here: "And because he did a disgraceful act,"
and it is written there:
"Because she did a disgraceful act in ישראל."
phrases.notes: דברים 22:21, about a נערה המאורסה who sinned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the textual source for step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That עכן's 'נבלה' was relations with a נערה המאורסה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The identical phrase 'עשה נבלה בישראל' in יהושע 7:15 and דברים 22:21.

steps.title: Isn't this teaching obvious too?
steps.stepSummary: Again the גמרא asks why we need this teaching, since עכן already broke the whole תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבא בר זבדא's teaching. This is the same kind of question it asked in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If עכן broke all five חומשי תורה, the איסור of a נערה המאורסה should already be included. So the special teaching seems unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: The man who took from the forbidden spoils of יריחו
The five books of the תורה

phrases.english: That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same challenge as step 7, now aimed at step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא בר זבדא's teaching about the נערה המאורסה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Breaking all five חומשים already includes this איסור.

steps.title: We might think he did not go that far
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought עכן would not sink to such a low level, so the teaching was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said he did not throw himself away that much. So it teaches us that he did.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 11 the same way it answered step 7. We might have assumed this sin was too extreme even for עכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sin with a נערה המאורסה is a very severe איסור. It carries the death penalty of סקילה. Without the teaching, we might have thought עכן stopped short of it.

keyTerms.meaning: To such an extent; this much
He abandoned himself; he let himself go completely

steps.whatToRemember: Twice the גמרא asks פשיטא, and twice it answers מהו דתימא. Each teaching shows that עכן fell lower than we would have guessed.

phrases.english: You might have said
he did not abandon himself to such an extent,
so it teaches us (that he did).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ruling out a mistaken assumption (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עכן would not go so far as a sin with a נערה המאורסה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He did go that far, so the teaching is needed.

steps.title: רבינא: the link teaches his punishment, סקילה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reads the same גזירה שוה as teaching that עכן's punishment was like that of a נערה המאורסה, which is סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: His punishment is like that of a betrothed young woman, which is by stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a different reading of the same link between the two פסוקים. For him, it does not teach what עכן did. It teaches how he was punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אבא בר זבדא, the shared words reveal a sin. For רבינא, they reveal a death penalty. A נערה המאורסה who sins gets סקילה, so עכן got סקילה too.

keyTerms.meaning: Stoning, one of the four court death penalties

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not adding another sin to עכן's list. He reads the same גזירה שוה as teaching only the type of punishment.

phrases.english: רבינא said:
His punishment is like that of a betrothed young woman,
which is by stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different use of the גזירה שוה from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזירה שוה teaches that עכן was punished with סקילה, like a נערה המאורסה.

steps.title: Why were עכן's children punished?
steps.stepSummary: The ריש גלותא quotes the פסוק listing everything taken with עכן and asks: if he sinned, what did his sons and daughters do wrong?
steps.simpleTranslation: The ריש גלותא said to רב הונא: It is written, 'And יהושע took עכן son of זרח, the silver, the cloak, the bar of gold, his sons, his daughters, his ox, his donkey, his sheep, his tent, and all that he had.' If he sinned, what did his sons and daughters sin?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. The ריש גלותא quotes the פסוק to set up a hard question: it seems innocent children were punished along with their father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists עכן's sons and daughters together with his property, as if they shared his fate. But the תורה says children do not die for a parent's sin. So how could this be? The next step gives רב הונא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the head of the Jewish community in בבל

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: The ריש גלותא said to רב הונא:

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב: ״וַיִּקַּח יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֶת עָכָן בֶּן זֶרַח
phrases.english: It is written: "And יהושע took עכן son of זרח,
phrases.notes: יהושע 7:24

phrases.english: and the silver, and the cloak,
and the bar of gold,
and his sons, and his daughters,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת שׁוֹרוֹ וְאֶת חֲמֹרוֹ וְאֶת צֹאנוֹ
phrases.english: and his ox, and his donkey, and his sheep,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת אׇהֳלוֹ וְאֶת כׇּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ״.
phrases.english: and his tent, and all that he had."
If he sinned,
what did his sons and daughters sin?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא לְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the פסוק describing עכן's punishment.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק in יהושע 7:24, which seems to include עכן's children in his punishment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Children should not be punished for their father's sin, yet the פסוק seems to punish them with him.

steps.title: כל ישראל was there too, so the family was only there to learn a lesson
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers the ריש גלותא. כל ישראל also went to the valley, and they surely did nothing wrong. They were brought only to be shocked into obeying, and the same is true of עכן's sons and daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: By your logic, if עכן sinned, what did כל ישראל do wrong? The פסוק says 'and כל ישראל with him.' Instead, they were brought there to be taught a lesson. In the same way, his children were brought there to be taught a lesson.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the ריש גלותא's question from the last step by pointing out that the same פסוק also says כל ישראל went along.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ריש גלותא assumed that anyone taken to the valley with עכן was punished. רב הונא shows this cannot be right, because the whole nation came too and they were innocent. So being taken there does not mean being punished. It means watching the punishment and learning to fear sin.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turning the questioner's own logic back on him
To discipline them, to shake them up so they learn a lesson
So too, the same applies here

steps.whatToRemember: עכן's children were not killed. They were brought along, like the rest of ישראל, only to see the punishment and learn from it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume everyone 'taken with עכן' was punished. The גמרא's point is that the family was there only as onlookers, just like the whole nation.

phrases.english: He said to him: And according to your reasoning,
phrases.notes: The one answering the ריש גלותא here is רב הונא.

phrases.aramaic: אִם הוּא חָטָא – כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל מֶה חָטְאוּ?
phrases.english: if he sinned, what did all of Israel sin?
As it is written: "And all Israel with him."
phrases.notes: יהושע 7:24

phrases.english: Rather, it was to discipline them.
So too, it was in order to discipline them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ריש גלותא's question about why עכן's sons and daughters were taken.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turns the questioner's logic around (ליטעמיך) and reinterprets the purpose of being taken along
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone taken to the valley with עכן was punished, including his children.
steps.terutzMaskana: The family, like all Israel, was taken only to watch and be frightened into obedience.

steps.title: Was עכן punished with both burning and stoning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that says they burned them and stoned them, and asks whether he really got two death penalties.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.' With two punishments?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about עכן's punishment and asks a short question about it. This sets up רבינא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person is not normally put to death in two ways. The פסוק seems to describe both burning and stoning, so the גמרא wants to know how to understand it.

phrases.english: "And they burned them with fire,
and they stoned them with stones."
phrases.notes: יהושע 7:25

phrases.english: With two?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new detail of עכן's punishment, connected to רבינא's earlier point that the punishment was סקילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוק can mention both burning and stoning for one punishment.

steps.title: Burning was for the things, stoning was for the living
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that each item got what suited it. Whatever was fit to be burned was burned, and whatever was fit to be stoned was stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: What was fit for burning went to burning, and what was fit for stoning went to stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question by splitting the פסוק between two kinds of things that were punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two verbs do not describe two death penalties for one person. Burning applied to the objects, and stoning applied to the living beings. This fits רבינא's earlier statement that עכן's own punishment was סקילה.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
what was fit for burning went to burning,
what was fit for stoning went to stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of 'with two?'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each item got the punishment suited to it: objects were burned and living things were stoned.

steps.title: What was the 'mantle of שנער'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes עכן's confession about the fine mantle he took. רב says it was a cloak of fine wool, and שמואל says it was a garment dyed with alum.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And I saw among the spoil one fine mantle of שנער and two hundred shekels of silver.' רב said: a cloak of fine wool. שמואל said: a garment dyed with alum.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains one word in עכן's confession and brings two opinions about what the stolen garment was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls it a 'mantle of שנער' without saying what made it special. רב says the material was special, since it was choice wool. שמואל says the dye was special, since it was colored with alum.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloak made of fine wool

phrases.english: "And I saw among the spoil
one fine mantle of Shinar
and two hundred shekels of silver."
phrases.notes: יהושע 7:21. This is עכן's own confession.

phrases.english: Rav said: a cloak of fine wool,
and Shmuel said: a garment dyed with alum.

steps.triggerLanguage: וָאֵרֶא בַשָּׁלָל אַדֶּרֶת שִׁנְעָר אַחַת טוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to explain a word in עכן's confession.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the mantle was fine wool. שמואל: it was a garment dyed with alum.

steps.title: יהושע throws the stolen items before ה׳ and complains
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains 'ויציקום' to mean that יהושע threw the stolen things down before ה׳. He asked whether the majority of the סנהדרין should die over such small things, and he pointed to the 'about thirty-six men' killed at העי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they laid them out before ה׳‎.' רב נחמן said: He came and threw them down before ה׳. He said before Him: Master of the World, should the majority of the סנהדרין be killed over these? As it says: 'And the men of העי struck about thirty-six men of them.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן reads the word 'ויציקום' as a strong action. יהושע threw the items down and argued with ה׳ that the loss at העי was too great for such small things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain פסוק says the items were simply laid out. רב נחמן reads it as יהושע throwing them down in protest. His complaint depends on the 'about thirty-six' who died at העי being 'the majority of the סנהדרין'. The next steps explain how that is understood.

keyTerms.meaning: And they laid them out (or poured them out)
The city of העי, where Israel lost a battle because of עכן's sin

phrases.english: "And they laid them out before ה׳."
phrases.notes: יהושע 7:23

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
He came and threw them down before ה׳.
phrases.notes: 'He' is יהושע.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the World,
over these things should there be killed
the majority of the Sanhedrin?
As it is written: "And the men of Ai struck of them
about thirty-six men."
phrases.notes: יהושע 7:5. Thirty-six is more than half of the 71 members of the סנהדרין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: בָּא וַחֲבָטָם לִפְנֵי הַמָּקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in the story, about the stolen items being laid before ה׳.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע threw the stolen items before ה׳ and protested that the majority of the סנהדרין died because of them.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: exactly thirty-six men died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the 'majority of the סנהדרין' claim. רבי יהודה says thirty-six men were actually killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא taught: Thirty-six, actually. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to explain how 'about thirty-six men' matches 'the majority of the סנהדרין'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the number is meant literally: thirty-six men died. That is more than half of the 71 members of the סנהדרין, which supports רב נחמן's wording.

phrases.english: And it was taught: thirty-six, actually,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's claim that the dead equaled the majority of the סנהדרין.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's claim that the majority of the סנהדרין was killed at העי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה that exactly thirty-six died

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: it was one man, יאיר בן מנשה
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה points out that the פסוק says 'about thirty-six', not exactly thirty-six. He explains that only one great man, יאיר בן מנשה, was killed, and he was worth as much as the majority of the סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said to him: Were there really thirty-six? The פסוק only says 'about thirty-six men'! Rather, this is יאיר בן מנשה, who was equal to the majority of the סנהדרין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה rejects רבי יהודה's literal reading and gives his own explanation of the word 'about'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'about' tells רבי נחמיה that this is not an exact count of bodies. It means one person who was 'like' thirty-six: יאיר בן מנשה, whose importance equaled the majority of the סנהדרין. Either way, רב נחמן's complaint holds, since the loss equaled the majority of the סנהדרין.

keyTerms.meaning: A great leader from the tribe of מנשה
Equal in weight or worth to

steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions agree the loss at העי equaled 'the majority of the סנהדרין'. רבי יהודה says thirty-six men died, and רבי נחמיה says one man, יאיר בן מנשה, died who was worth that much.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי נחמיה does not argue with רב נחמן's complaint. He only disagrees with רבי יהודה about how many people actually died.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one small word, 'about', in a פסוק can be read as a hint to a deeper idea: one great person can be worth many others.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya said to him:
And were there really thirty-six?
But doesn't the פסוק say nothing
other than "about thirty-six men"!
Rather, this is Yair son of Menashe,
who was equal to the majority of the Sanhedrin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה: וְכִי שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשִׁשָּׁה הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה's literal reading of the number thirty-six.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only רבי יהודה's literal count, not the idea that the loss equaled the majority of the סנהדרין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק says 'about thirty-six', which does not fit an exact count.

steps.title: The poor man pleads and the rich man answers harshly: משה and יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רב reads משלי 18:23 as a contrast: משה spoke to ה׳ with soft pleading, and יהושע spoke to ה׳ harshly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: What does the פסוק mean, 'The poor man speaks pleadings, and the rich man answers harshly'? 'The poor man speaks pleadings' is משה. 'The rich man answers harshly' is יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן quotes רב, who explains a פסוק in משלי as describing two leaders. משה spoke to ה׳ gently, and יהושע spoke strongly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the earlier steps about יהושע and the sin of עכן. רב says יהושע's way of speaking to ה׳ was 'harsh,' but he does not yet say which words show it. The next steps look for that proof.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rav said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"The poor man speaks pleadings,
but the rich man answers harshly"?
phrases.notes: משלי 18:23

phrases.english: "The poor man speaks pleadings": this is Moshe.
"But the rich man answers harshly": this is Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַב: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from how many people died at העי to a new teaching about how יהושע spoke to ה׳.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In משלי 18:23, the 'poor man' who pleads is משה and the 'rich man' who answers harshly is יהושע.

steps.title: Where do we see that יהושע spoke harshly? A first suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what shows יהושע's harshness. It suggests the proof is that he threw the stolen items down before ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason we call יהושע harsh? If you say it is because the פסוק says 'And they laid them out before ה׳,' and רב נחמן explained that he came and threw them down before ה׳...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רב's claim and offers a first possible answer. This sets up the challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested proof is רב נחמן's teaching from step 19: יהושע threw the stolen items down before ה׳ in a forceful protest. The word אִילֵּימָא ('if you say') tells us this suggestion is about to be pushed back.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that will soon be challenged)

phrases.english: What is the reason?
If you say it is because it is written:
"And they laid them out before ה׳,"
phrases.notes: יהושע 7:23. This is the same teaching from step 19.

phrases.english: and Rav Nachman said:
he came and threw them down before ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual basis of the claim made in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words or actions show that יהושע spoke harshly to ה׳?

steps.title: פינחס did the same thing, so throwing things down cannot be the proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion. פינחס also threw the sinners down before ה׳ and argued with Him, and he is not called harsh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did פינחס not do the same? The פסוק says 'פינחס stood up and ויפלל, and the plague stopped.' רבי אלעזר said: It does not say 'he prayed' but 'ויפלל,' which teaches that he made a kind of court case with his Creator. He threw them down before ה׳ and said: Master of the World, should 24,000 Jews fall because of these people? As it says, 'And those who died in the plague were 24,000.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggestion by pointing to פינחס, who did the very same thing. So that action cannot be what makes יהושע 'harsh.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads the unusual word וַיְפַלֵּל as making a case (פְּלִילוּת) against ה׳ rather than simply praying. Since פינחס also threw the sinners down and protested, and he is praised for it, throwing things down cannot be what makes יהושע different.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a challenge)
And he made judgment, argued his case

phrases.english: Is that to say that Pinchas did not do the same?
As it is written: "Pinchas stood up and made judgment,
and the plague was stopped."
phrases.notes: תהלים 106:30

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
It does not say "and he prayed";
rather it says "vayefalel."
This teaches that he made a court case with his Creator.
He came and threw them down before ה׳,
phrases.notes: "Them" means זמרי and כזבי, the two sinners פינחס killed.

phrases.english: and said before Him: Master of the World,
because of these, should there fall
twenty-four thousand of Israel?
As it is written: "And those who died in the plague were
twenty-four thousand."
phrases.notes: במדבר 25:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggested proof from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that throwing the stolen items before ה׳ shows יהושע's harshness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פינחס did the same thing and is not called harsh, so that action cannot be what sets יהושע apart.

steps.title: A second suggestion: 'Why did You bring this nation over the ירדן?'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests instead that יהושע's harshness shows in his complaint, 'Why did You bring this nation over the ירדן?'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is from here: 'Why did You bring this nation over the ירדן?'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first proof failed, the גמרא offers a new one: יהושע's words of complaint to ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof moves from יהושע's action to his words. Asking 'why did You do this?' sounds like a complaint against ה׳.

phrases.english: Rather, it is from here:
"Why did You bring
this nation over the Jordan?"
phrases.notes: יהושע 7:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof that was rejected in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source for the same claim
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The proof was יהושע throwing the items down.
steps.terutzMaskana: The proof is יהושע's complaint, 'Why did You bring us over?'

steps.title: משה said something similar, so this cannot be the proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second suggestion. משה also said 'Why have You done bad to this people?' and he is called the gentle one.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה also said: 'Why have You done bad to this people?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: משה used the same kind of 'why' language, and he is the one called the pleading poor man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If asking 'why' made someone harsh, then משה would be harsh too. But the פסוק in משלי calls משה the gentle one, so the 'why' question cannot be what marks יהושע as harsh.

phrases.english: Moshe also said:
"Why have You done bad to this people?"
phrases.notes: שמות 5:22

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new proof offered in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that 'Why did You bring this nation over' shows harshness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה said a similar 'why' sentence, yet he is the gentle one, so this cannot be what makes יהושע harsh.

steps.title: The real proof: 'If only we had stayed on the other side of the ירדן'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finds the real proof in the rest of יהושע's words: 'If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the ירדן.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is from here: 'If only we had been content and stayed on the other side of the ירדן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles on the continuation of the same פסוק as the true sign of יהושע's harsh words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה never said anything like this. Wishing they had never entered ארץ ישראל goes beyond asking 'why'; it sounds like regretting ה׳'s whole plan. That is what makes it 'harsh.'

keyTerms.meaning: We had been content, we had agreed
The other side of the Jordan

steps.whatToRemember: The 'harsh' words of יהושע were not throwing the items down (פינחס did that) and not asking 'why' (משה did that). They were his wish that the people had stayed on the other side of the ירדן.

phrases.english: Rather, it is from here:
"If only we had been content and stayed
on the other side of the Jordan."
phrases.notes: These words come later in the same פסוק, יהושע 7:7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof that was rejected in step 26 and closes the search.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source for the same claim
steps.terutzMaskana: The proof is יהושע's wish that they had stayed on the other side of the ירדן.

steps.title: ה׳ tells יהושע: your failing is worse than theirs
steps.stepSummary: רבי שילא explains 'Get up' (יהושע 7:10): ה׳ told יהושע that his own failing was worse, because they were commanded to set up stones once they crossed the ירדן, and they had already gone sixty מיל without doing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And ה׳ said to יהושע: Get up.' רבי שילא taught: ה׳ said to him, 'Yours is worse than theirs. I said, "When you cross the ירדן, set up the stones," and you have already gone sixty מיל away.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שילא explains ה׳'s answer to יהושע‎. ה׳ tells him that the leaders' own failure is worse than the sin of the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע was complaining about the people's loss, but ה׳ points to a failing of יהושע himself. They were told to set up stones right after crossing the ירדן, yet they had traveled sixty מיל without doing it.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of distance, about a kilometer

steps.confusionAlert: 'Yours is worse than theirs' does not mean יהושע took from the forbidden spoils. It means the failure to set up the stones after crossing the ירדן was more serious than the sin of עכן.

phrases.english: "And ה׳ said to Yehoshua: Get up."
phrases.notes: יהושע 7:10

phrases.english: Rabbi Sheila taught:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:
Yours is worse than theirs.
I said:
"And it will be, when you cross the Jordan, you shall set up,"
phrases.notes: דברים 27:4. What they were told to set up was the stones.

phrases.english: and you have gone sixty mil away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from יהושע's words to ה׳'s answer to him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ told יהושע that his own failing was worse than the people's sin, because they went sixty מיל past the ירדן without setting up the stones as commanded.

steps.title: רב teaches that יהושע left nothing undone
steps.stepSummary: After רבי שילא leaves, רב brings a פסוק showing that יהושע did everything משה commanded.
steps.simpleTranslation: After רבי שילא went out, רב set up a speaker beside himself and taught: 'As ה׳ commanded משה His servant, so משה commanded יהושע, and so יהושע did. He left nothing undone of all that ה׳ commanded משה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a public teaching that quietly pushes back on רבי שילא's explanation from Step 28.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שילא said יהושע failed by not setting up the stones right after crossing the ירדן. רב quotes a פסוק saying יהושע did everything he was commanded. So, according to רב, יהושע could not have neglected the stones.

keyTerms.meaning: A speaker who repeats the teacher's words out loud to the crowd
He taught or expounded a פסוק
He did not leave out anything

phrases.english: After he went out,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי שילא, who just finished his teaching in Step 28.

phrases.english: Rav set up a speaker beside himself
and taught:
"As ה׳ commanded Moshe His servant,
so did Moshe command Yehoshua,
and so did Yehoshua do;
he left nothing undone

phrases.aramaic: מִכׇּל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה׳ אֶת מֹשֶׁה״.
phrases.english: of all that ה׳ commanded Moshe."
phrases.notes: יהושע 11:15

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּתַר דִּנְפַק, אוֹקֵים רַב אָמוֹרָא עֲלֵיהּ וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing reading that undercuts רבי שילא's charge against יהושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע did everything he was commanded, so he did not neglect setting up the stones.

steps.title: Then why does ה׳ say 'Get up'?
steps.stepSummary: If יהושע did nothing wrong, what does 'Get up' come to teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'Get up'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב. If יהושע was perfect, the words 'Get up' still seem to blame him for something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Get up' (יהושע 7:10) sounds like a rebuke to יהושע himself. If he left nothing undone, the rebuke seems to have no target. רב now has to explain what 'Get up' means.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the פסוק come to teach?

phrases.english: If so,
what does the verse mean by "Get you up"?
phrases.notes: יהושע 7:10, the same words רבי שילא explained in Step 28.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's teaching from Step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that יהושע did everything right
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Get up' implies that יהושע himself was at fault, which does not fit a flawless יהושע.

steps.title: You caused them to sin
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ told יהושע that he caused the people's sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: ה׳ said to him: You caused it for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. 'Get up' does not refer to the stones. It means יהושע caused the people to sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע did not break any command. But a decision he made led the people to stumble. The next step shows which decision.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: ה׳ is speaking to יהושע.

phrases.english: You caused it for them.
phrases.notes: Meaning, you caused their sin. The next line hints at how.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 30.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Get up' must mean יהושע broke a command, such as delaying the stones.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Get up' means יהושע caused the people's sin, without breaking any command.

steps.title: Proof from ה׳'s command at עי
steps.stepSummary: ה׳'s command at עי shows how יהושע caused the sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what ה׳ told him at עי: 'Do to עי and its king as you did to יריחו and its king,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב's answer with ה׳'s later command about the city of עי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At עי‎, ה׳ lets the people keep the spoils. This hints that the strict ban on יריחו's spoils was יהושע's own decision. That ban is what led to the sin of taking from them.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is meant when it says

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a leader can carry blame for the people's sin even when he broke no command.

phrases.english: And this is what He said to him at Ai:
"And you shall do to Ai and her king
as you did to Jericho and her king, etc."
phrases.notes: יהושע 8:2. The 'etc.' goes on: 'only its spoil and its cattle you may take for yourselves.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 31.
steps.raayaObject: That יהושע caused the people's sin
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע 8:2, where ה׳ lets them keep the spoils of עי

steps.title: יהושע bows to the captain of ה׳'s army
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק where יהושע meets the angel near יריחו and bows down.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'When יהושע was by יריחו, he lifted his eyes and looked... He said: No, I am the captain of ה׳'s army, I have now come. And יהושע fell on his face to the ground and bowed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new פסוק about יהושע. It is setting up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע meets an unknown figure and bows to him. The figure calls himself the captain of ה׳'s army. The detail that matters is that יהושע greeted a stranger.

phrases.english: "And it came to pass when Joshua was by Jericho
that he lifted up his eyes and looked, etc.
phrases.notes: יהושע 5:13. He saw a man with a drawn sword and asked whose side he was on.

phrases.english: And he said: No, but

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי שַׂר צְבָא ה׳ עַתָּה בָאתִי
phrases.english: I am captain of the host of the Lord; I have now come.
[And Joshua fell on his face to the earth and bowed down.]"
phrases.notes: יהושע 5:14. The words in square brackets finish the פסוק in the corrected text.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about יהושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע bowed to a figure who said he was the captain of ה׳'s army.

steps.title: Greeting a stranger at night is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: How could יהושע greet a stranger, when רבי יוחנן forbids greeting someone at night in case he is a שד?
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he do this? Doesn't רבי יוחנן say that a person may not greet his fellow at night, because we worry he may be a שד?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges יהושע's behavior using a rule from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says not to greet someone you don't recognize at night, because he might be a שד. The גמרא understands that יהושע met this figure at night. So how could יהושע bow to him?

phrases.english: How could he do so?
But doesn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
It is forbidden for a person
to greet his fellow at night,
since we are concerned that perhaps he is a demon!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges יהושע's act from Step 33.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's rule forbids greeting an unknown figure at night because it might be a שד.

steps.title: The stranger mentioned ה׳
steps.stepSummary: This case was different, because the stranger said he was the captain of ה׳'s army.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because he told him: 'I am the captain of ה׳'s army, I have now come.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that יהושע had a reason to trust this figure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually you cannot tell who a stranger is at night. Here the figure named himself and mentioned ה׳. That made this meeting different from the case רבי יוחנן worries about.

phrases.english: It is different there,
since he said to him:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֲנִי שַׂר צְבָא ה׳ עַתָּה בָאתִי וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: "I am captain of the host of the Lord; I have now come, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 34.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יהושע greeted an unknown figure who could have been a שד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The figure named himself using ה׳'s name, so this case is an exception.

steps.title: Maybe the שד was lying
steps.stepSummary: Couldn't a שד lie about who it is?
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they lie?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. A שד could simply claim to be an angel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 35 relied on what the figure said about himself. But a lying שד could say the same thing, so his claim alone should not be enough.

phrases.english: But perhaps they lie?
phrases.notes: 'They' are שדים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: Trusting the figure's claim about himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שד could falsely claim to be an angel.

steps.title: שדים do not say ה׳'s name for nothing
steps.stepSummary: There is a tradition that שדים do not say ה׳'s name in vain.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have learned as a tradition that they do not say ה׳'s name for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question with a known tradition about שדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the figure mentioned ה׳, the tradition tells us he was not a lying שד. So יהושע was right to trust him and bow.
steps.whatToRemember: יהושע could bow to the stranger because he used ה׳'s name, and שדים do not say ה׳'s name for nothing.

phrases.english: It is learned as a tradition that they do not utter
the name of Heaven in vain.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמִירִי דְּלָא מַפְּקִי שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם לְבַטָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 36.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שד could lie about being an angel.
steps.terutzMaskana: שדים do not use ה׳'s name in vain, so the figure's words could be trusted.
